verifiedSemantics: Indexer reads normalized query low rank, independently projects an index key from x, applies LayerNorm/rotary/Hadamard and FP8 activation quantization. Its cache has distinct FP8 payload and FP32 scale tensors; scale_fmt rounding does not make the scale storage one byte.

FP8 index scans every prefix key. Its kernel rectifies each head dot product, multiplies query weights, reduces heads, applies the key scale and writes one FP32 score per query/key. Top-K uses min(index_topk,end_pos); indices are forward-local, not a carried decode state.
The released MLA decode demo computes full-prefix latent/rotary QK and full-prefix AV, then uses a dense index mask around softmax. Top-K selection alone does not reduce those einsum costs.

The decode demo keeps normalized/fake-FP8-rounded latent KV in BF16 plus a separate rotary key cache. Query absorption and output expansion use disjoint key/value slices of wkv_b. RMSNorm weights and index LayerNorm weight/bias are FP32. Index weights_proj is FP32 in this implementation.
The fixed inference config uses 128 attention heads, 64 index heads, index dimension 128 and K=2048, with FP8 checkpoint matrices. Buffers use maximum batch/sequence allocation.
authoredAssumptions: Decode-only single-query MLA attention fragment, without block input norm/residual, FFN, embeddings or full language-model costs. Artificial H=8, attention heads=2, query rank=4, latent rank=8, nonrotary/rotary/value dimensions=4/2/4, index heads=2 and index dimension/block=8/8. This reduced block is not source-kernel compatible.

All ordinary projection weights and arithmetic use BF16 rather than the fixed FP8 checkpoint matrices. Index weights_proj stays FP32; index dots use FP8 E4M3 inputs with FP32 accumulation. BF16 main scores/probabilities follow the demo. Norm/rotary/Hadamard/selection use explicit FP32 vector proxies with on-chip internal workspace; BF16/FP32 and FP8 conversions add execution-only work.

source-mask follows full-prefix demo arithmetic, with materialized BF16 score components and dense FP32 index mask. sparse-gather is a separately authored theoretical kernel path with explicit shared BF16 selected-KV/PE staging and selected QK/AV; it is not a claim that the released demo executes such kernels. dense is a no-indexer counterfactual, not output-equivalent attention.

FP8 index kernel intermediates stay on chip; one full-prefix FP32 score tensor is materialized. Per-head rectification, weighting, reduction and key-scale multiplication remain explicit arithmetic in the same leaf. Top-K proxy costs L*(min(K,L)+2) per request. Debug clone/broadcast/equality checks and network are omitted on this single-device fragment.

Dynamic buffers reserve call-end C+1 rows; provisioned buffers reserve M rows, reject C+1>M, and separately report active context. Index payload uses one byte per channel and each scale occupies four bytes. Two disjoint BF16 key/value weight slices sum to the original wkv_b size; no duplicate persistent dequantized weights. Warm history is initialized; no allocator slack or implicit migration cost.

Artificial 4096-byte device: BF16 matrix 1000, FP8 matrix 2000, FP32 matrix 500, FP32 vector 1000 operations/s; HBM 100 bytes/s. Serial, ideal main/index streams and declared-HBM sharing use the existing engine, exact precision classes and last-use liveness. No measured speed or accuracy claim.
